title: main-is-fast-forward-of-dev checks CONTAINMENT, not fast-forwardness — a rewind of main passes
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-15 in a local scratch repo, with the constructed git state asserted BEFORE
the verdict was read. Nothing was pushed to origin.

ci.yml:295 `main-is-fast-forward-of-dev` runs on every push to main and asserts exactly one
thing:

    git merge-base --is-ancestor "${{ github.sha }}" origin/dev

That is CONTAINMENT: "main's new HEAD is a commit dev already held". The job is NAMED
"main is fast-forward of dev", which is a strictly stronger property, and the job never
looks at where main WAS. `github.event.before` is not read.

THE HOLE. Rewind main to an older commit that is still on dev. The new HEAD is an ancestor
of origin/dev, so the guard is GREEN, while commits come OFF main:

    dev tip (c4)        = bbf1c8cefb827b7940aa0d44a06af41a9f6fbeba
    rewind target (c2)  = 2fbcd7973916f1817e167c11677f348443a0caca
    main after rewind   = 2fbcd7973916f1817e167c11677f348443a0caca   (asserted, not assumed)

    guard's check   `merge-base --is-ancestor c2 dev`  -> GREEN
    a real ff check `merge-base --is-ancestor c4 c2`   -> RED (c4 is not an ancestor of c2)

Both halves of prove-it-rejects and prove-it-accepts are already satisfied by this job: a
genuine promotion is green, the merge button is red. The case that finds it is the third
question -- does the NAME claim more than the BODY measures -- which neither half asks.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY. The job's own comment says it is "the guard that matters
most for this repo specifically: main carries zero branch rules here, so nothing else stands
between a bad push and main". A rewind is precisely the bad push it is the last line against,
and it is the one shape it cannot see.

THE CLAIM IS REPEATED OUTSIDE THE BODY, WITHOUT THE CAVEAT. CLAUDE.md's repo profile names
the job as "main is fast-forward of dev" when explaining why the two promotion guards are
deliberately not required contexts. A reader takes the guarantee from the name.

FIX SHAPE. Also assert the OLD main is an ancestor of the new one -- `git merge-base
--is-ancestor "$BEFORE" "$AFTER"` -- skipping when before is all-zeros (branch creation).
Keep the containment check; it catches a different thing (a foreign commit). Two assertions,
two messages.

AND EXTRACT IT. The job is inline shell, so it is untestable by construction and has never
had a test; that is why this survived. Extract to scripts/ and drive both branches against
local fixture repos, the way test/readme-readback.test.ts now does for A4 (LCLI-510).

METHODOLOGY NOTE, from opum-marketplace, and it cost them two false verdicts: zsh reads the
`:r` in "$SHA:refs/heads/main" as a variable modifier and pushes a garbage refspec, and
double quotes do NOT protect it. Use ${SHA}:refs/heads/main or run under bash, and assert the
resulting git state before trusting any verdict -- otherwise a proof that a gate reported on
an object it never measured is itself a measurement of an object that was never built.

PROVENANCE. Found by generalising LCLI-510's review: opum-marketplace reported the identical
defect in their promotion-guards.yml (OMARK-58) and named this repo's guard as a likely second
host. Verified here rather than inherited. opum-cli-e2e independently hit the same class
(TASK-74): a required check named "qualification matrix vs the committed baseline" that has
not compared against a baseline since 2026-09-07.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A rewind of main to an older commit that is still on dev makes the guard RED, proved against a constructed local repo whose state is asserted before the verdict is read
A genuine fast-forward promotion is still GREEN, proved separately — the accepting half, not inferred from the rejecting one
A foreign commit on main (the merge-button case) is still RED, so the existing containment check is kept rather than replaced
The assertion lives in scripts/ with a test that drives every branch against local fixture repos, because inline workflow shell is untestable by construction and that is why this survived
The job name and CLAUDE.md's repo-profile reference both describe what the body actually measures, or the body is widened to match the name

implementationNotes:
SEVERITY RESOLVED FOR THIS REPO, measured 2026-09-15 rather than cited from CLAUDE.md.

opum-marketplace found this same assertion in EIGHT repositories (opum-agent
promotion-guards.yml:52, opum-doc :73, quest-cli promotion-guardrails.yml:59,
opum-cli-e2e :59, lore-web ci.yml:207, quest-web check.yml:206, opum-marketplace,
and here), byte-identical in the six they read, and none of the eight mentions
github.event.before or github.event.forced. They flagged severity as UNEVEN rather
than ruling on it, because theirs sits behind a tier-3 rail and is therefore
defense-in-depth failing open, and they had not checked anyone else's branch rules.

Checked ours. Three independent reads, all agreeing:

    gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/rules/branches/main        -> []
    gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/branches/main/protection   -> 404 Branch not protected
    gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/branches/main --jq .protected -> false

(dev, by contrast, carries exactly one rule: required_status_checks.)

So main here has NO ruleset, NO classic protection, and force-push is not blocked at
the platform level. This guard is not defense-in-depth in lore-cli -- it is the only
automated thing that was supposed to notice, and the one shape it cannot see is the
rewind. That makes this repo the severe instance of the eight, and it is why the job's
own comment calls it "the guard that matters most for this repo specifically".

Recorded so the next reader does not re-derive it, and so nobody downgrades this by
analogy to a sibling whose main IS protected. Severity is per-repo here; the assertion
is identical, the consequence is not.

CROSS-REPO HALF IS NOT OURS. opum-marketplace routed the fleet-wide fix to opum-agent,
because the shape is documented in opum-doc's promote-dev-to-main runbook and patching
copies without fixing the source reproduces it at the next repo. LCLI-514 is the lore-cli
half only. Do not edit a sibling's workflow.

CORRECTION TO THE NOTE ABOVE: it is the severe THREE, not the severe one.

The previous note ended "that makes this repo the severe instance of the eight",
correctly bounded at the time -- I had measured lore-cli and opum-marketplace had
measured opum-marketplace, and I said so. The bound was the honest part; the
singular was still wrong, and a reader who skipped the caveat would have carried
away an exclusivity nobody had measured.

opum-agent ran the per-repo survey at 2026-09-15 23:28Z, `rules/branches/main`
length and `branches/main.protected`:

    opum-agent        rules=1  protected=true
    opum-doc          rules=1  protected=true
    quest-cli         rules=1  protected=true
    opum-cli-e2e      rules=1  protected=true
    opum-marketplace  rules=1  protected=true
    lore-web          rules=0  protected=FALSE
    quest-web         rules=0  protected=FALSE
    lore-cli          rules=0  protected=FALSE

THREE of the eight have an unprotected main. In each of those three this guard is
the only automated thing that was supposed to notice, and the shape it cannot see
is the rewind.

PROVENANCE, because a relayed measurement is still a hypothesis until someone says
who resolved it. The lore-cli row is MINE, read first-hand three ways (rules ->
[], protection -> 404, .protected -> false). The other seven rows are opum-agent's,
not re-resolved here. What raises confidence in theirs is that their lore-cli row
agrees exactly with my independent read, so the method matches on the one row where
both exist -- that is evidence about their method, not proof of the other six rows.
Anyone acting on the lore-web or quest-web rows should re-resolve them.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: this is still a per-repo severity fact, the assertion is still
identical across all eight, and lore-cli's exposure is unchanged by having company.

THIRD CORRECTION, and this one invalidates a COLUMN rather than a row.

The note above reproduced opum-agent's survey as "the other five carry rules=1,
protected=true", which reads as "those five are safe from this". It does not
support that. opum-cli-e2e measured their own ruleset after being reported as
protected on the strength of rules=1, and found `required_status_checks` ONLY --
no `non_fast_forward` rule. opum-marketplace had made the same inference and
corrected it.

The mechanism, which is the part that generalises: a rewind pushes a commit that
ALREADY carries green required contexts, because the earlier promotion is what put
them there. So a required-status-checks rule cannot refuse a rewind. The rule that
refuses one is `non_fast_forward`, and neither `rules/branches/<b>` length nor the
`protected` boolean tells you whether it is present.

Measured here 2026-09-15, since the question is now "which rule", not "how many":

    gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/rules/branches/dev --jq '[.[].type]'
        -> ["required_status_checks"]
    gh api repos/opum-ai/lore-cli/rulesets
        -> exactly one: 22838594 require-ci-on-dev, active, target branch
    ruleset 22838594 refs -> ["refs/heads/dev"], rules -> ["required_status_checks"]

So lore-cli has NO non_fast_forward rule anywhere: not on main, which has no rules
at all, and not on dev, whose single ruleset carries only required_status_checks.

TWO CONSEQUENCES.

1. lore-cli's own severity is UNCHANGED -- main was already rules=0. Everything in
   the first note stands. This correction is about the comparison, not about us.
2. The eight-repo split into "three exposed, five protected" is NOT ESTABLISHED.
   The five were classified by a metric that does not measure the property. They
   may be protected; nobody has measured `non_fast_forward` on them. Do not cite
   that split as a reason this is narrow.

This is the third time tonight a correctly-bounded summary of this survey carried a
stronger claim than its measurement: severe-one -> severe-three -> and now the
five-protected column itself. The recurring error is not sloppiness about caveats,
it is reaching for a number that is nearby and available (rule COUNT) instead of
the property actually in question (which RULE).
